title: Surinder Koli & Moninder Singh Pandher v. State of UP (Nithari Serial Murders)
crime_type: Serial Child Homicide / Abduction / Sexual Assault
court_or_authority: Supreme Court of India / Special CBI Court, Ghaziabad
source: Supreme Court of India Judgment & Indian Kanoon (doc/797079)
location: Nithari Village, Sector 31, Noida, Uttar Pradesh, India
evidence: Excavation and forensic retrieval of 19 skeletal remains and skulls from the municipal drainage canal behind bungalow D-5
Biological DNA matching of recovered bone fragments with parents of missing children
Section 164 CrPC judicial confession recorded before Metropolitan Magistrate detailing the sequence of luring and strangulation
Recovery of victim clothing and shoes concealed in residential pantry and attic
Recovery of cutting implements and saw blades corroborating dismemberment wounds
modus_operandi: Targeted impoverished children and young women walking near bungalow D-5 in Sector 31 Noida. Lured victims inside with food, sweets, or employment promises. Strangled victims from behind, followed by sexual assault, dismemberment of bodies, and disposal of remains in gunny sacks tossed into the rear drainage channel.
personality_disorder: Clinical and psychiatric examinations noted severe paraphilia, necrophilia, sadism, and antisocial personality traits characterized by complete moral dissociation and absence of guilt during judicial confession.
common_traits: Strangulation by ligature or physical asphyxiation
Dismemberment to hinder identification and transport remains
Disposal in subterranean municipal storm drains
summary: Landmark Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) inquiry into serial disappearances of children in Nithari village between 2005 and 2006. The Supreme Court of India upheld the conviction and capital sentence of Surinder Koli, establishing judicial precedent on circumstantial evidence and judicial confessions under Section 164 CrPC.
